Condo buildings in Cariboo
Barclay Woods — 9847 / 9857 / 9867 Manchester Drive

A Bosa-built wood-frame complex on 5 acres, in three buildings. Year built conflicts between sources: unit listings state 1980; the building directory page for 9867 Manchester states 1981 — treat the year as unresolved and confirm from the strata plan/Form B. A current listing title describes the 9857 building as a "271 Unit Development, Wood Frame" — whether 271 units is the whole complex or one phase is not confirmed. Published restrictions: pets allowed with restrictions (one listing specifies 1 cat or 1 dog); rentals allowed. Amenities: gym, social room, courtyard, shared laundry. Published capital work: windows 2013, plumbing 2014, common areas 2015, roof 2018.
Brookside Court — 9880 / 9890 Manchester Drive

Wood-frame, built 1982. A current listing title describes the 9880 building as a "99 Unit Development, Wood Frame" — whether that count covers both addresses is not confirmed. Published restrictions: one cat allowed, no dogs (per a current listing); a published rental position is not confirmed. Published capital work: rainscreen and re-piping 2025, windows 2019, elevator 2017. Amenities: fitness centre, sauna.
Brookside Park — 9584 Manchester Drive
Built 1981. Published restrictions: pets allowed, rentals allowed. Unit count: Not confirmed. Construction type: Not confirmed in the sources checked.
Strathmore Towers — 9603 / 9623 / 9633 Manchester Drive

Three concrete high-rises, built 1994 — the sub-area's only towers and its newest stock. Published restrictions: pets allowed, rentals allowed. Amenities: outdoor pool, hot tub, sauna, gym, tennis courts, concierge. Unit count: Not confirmed.
Streets, schools and getting around Cariboo

items.t: Cariboo is the north-east/east Burnaby sub-area around Cariboo Road and Cariboo Hill, inside the City's Cariboo-Armstrong planning area. Its residential streets run south from the Lougheed Highway corridor toward 16th Avenue and the New Westminster border side of east Burnaby.
The verified condo stock concentrates in one pocket: Manchester Drive, south of Lougheed Highway, where four wood-frame and concrete complexes sit together. That pocket is MLS-classified Cariboo.
Green anchors: Stoney Creek Park (2 tennis courts, 2 pickleball courts) and the Cariboo/Brunette River Conservation Lands on the north side.
Schools: Armstrong Elementary (8757 Armstrong Avenue), Cariboo Hill Secondary (8580 16th Avenue) and Lyndhurst Elementary (9847 Lyndhurst Street).

Recreation anchor in transition: the Cameron Community Centre is being replaced in a $267M project; the temporary Cameron operates inside The City of Lougheed shopping centre at 110-9855 Austin Avenue.
Transit: route 110 runs along the sub-area's north side. Whether a bus route runs on Cariboo Road itself is not verified.

blocks.text: Good to know about Cariboo

items.t: The secondary school is a heritage record with a build history. Cariboo Hill Secondary (8580 16th Avenue) is documented in the City's heritage record as built in 1961, with additions in 1969, 1971 and 1974 — a 1960s campus, not a modern one, whatever the playing fields suggest from the road.

The community centre is temporarily inside a mall. While the $267M Cameron replacement is built, the temporary Cameron Community Centre operates at 110-9855 Austin Avenue inside The City of Lougheed — buyers touring the area who look for a standalone centre will not find one yet.

September 2026 recorded zero detached listings and zero detached sales for Cariboo. The sub-area's entire recorded market that month was 23 condos & townhomes listings and 1 sale — pricing evidence here is thin by structure, not by week.

Two of the four complexes have already been through the big-ticket cycle. Brookside Court's rainscreen and re-piping were done in 2025 and Barclay Woods' roof in 2018 — the diligence question in this pocket is what remains (and what the depreciation report schedules next), not whether the buildings have been maintained at all.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Cariboo

items.t: City zoning — Burnaby's current bylaw only: The new bylaw carries an R1 Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing District and an R2 Townhouse District in its Part 3 district list. The Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan was adopted December 9, 2025 and replaces the 1998 OCP.

blocks.text: Good to know about Cariboo

items.t: One directory name, two built forms, two MLS sub-areas.

The green space is conservation land, not a manicured park. The City's park dedication bylaw dedicates the Cariboo and Brunette River Conservation Lands and the Stoney Creek Park and Trail System on the area's north side; Stoney Creek Park carries 2 tennis courts and 2 pickleball courts, and creek-side lots carry watercourse setbacks that travel with the creek, not the lot line.

Cariboo Hill Secondary dates the neighbourhood's growth era: the City's heritage record dates the school to 1961, built because Armstrong, Seaforth and Lyndhurst elementaries had grown, opening with 410 students and peaking at over 1,100 in 1974, with additions in 1969, 1971 and 1974.

The hospital is across the city, the urgent care is south-west: Burnaby Hospital, 3935 Kincaid St (Fraser Health), is west of Cariboo, and the Edmonds Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at #201-7315 Edmonds St in the Edmonds town centre.

There are no sub-area medians for Cariboo. SnapStats publishes medians at community level only, so any "Cariboo median" quoted from that report does not exist; the Burnaby Condos & Townhomes median ($686,000, September 2026) is the closest published figure and is a combined category.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Cariboo
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Historic lot fabric, not offerings: the neighbourhood's growth era is dated by its school anchor — Cariboo Hill Secondary was built in 1961 (additions 1969, 1971, 1974) because Armstrong, Seaforth and Lyndhurst elementaries had grown — which dates the subdivision era of the surrounding streets. That is built lot fabric history, not a claim that any historic lot is for sale.

Lot character: typical lot sizes are not verified at sub-area level — no official source read states them. The only sourced size figures are the R1 SSMUH thresholds in (280 m² / 281 m²), which are zoning thresholds, not a claim about any existing lot's size.

Serviced position: Burnaby's 2026 residential utility notice covers annual water, annual sewer use, a cross-connection device charge where applicable and a garbage toter fee, with the detached single-family water charge at $652.33 and sewer for single-family homes billed as a sewer parcel tax — the established streets sit inside that municipal system on the City's wording; servicing for any single parcel is confirmed with the City, not confirmed parcel-by-parcel here.
ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR parcel in Cariboo is confirmed; ALR status is a property-specific check through the Agricultural Land Commission. No ALR percentage split is stated.

Creek-side diligence: Stoney Creek and the Brunette River conservation lands run along the area's north side and are dedicated park by bylaw; a floodplain designation for Cariboo's residential streets was not confirmed in the sources read. Parcel-level hazard and watercourse-setback status are property-specific checks.

items.t: Cariboo is a City of Burnaby GVR board sub-area in north-east / east Burnaby around Cariboo Road and Cariboo Hill, between Lougheed Highway and the Edmonds side, anchored by Cariboo Hill Secondary and Armstrong Elementary; the City's heritage record for the secondary school places it in the "Cariboo-Armstrong" planning study area and the East Burnaby historic neighbourhood.

Main roads: Cariboo Road and Lougheed Highway, with Armstrong Avenue, 16th Avenue and Government Road linking west and south, and North Road forming the Coquitlam border to the east. Transit: route 110 runs between Lougheed Station and Metrotown Station via North Road, Cameron, Beaverbrook and Eastlake on the area's north side; Lougheed Station (Millennium and Evergreen lines) and Production Way–University Station are the SkyTrain stations on the north side; a bus route running on Cariboo Road itself: Not verified. Commute times in minutes: Not verified.

Civic anchors: Stoney Creek Park (2 tennis courts, 2 pickleball courts on the City's courts list) and the Cariboo and Brunette River Conservation Lands on the north side; the Cameron Community Centre and Library replacement is under construction at the Lougheed side ($267 million estimated total construction cost), with the Temporary Cameron operating inside The City of Lougheed Shopping Centre, 110-9855 Austin Avenue. Nearest hospital: Burnaby Hospital, 3935 Kincaid St, west across the city; Edmonds Urgent and Primary Care Centre at #201-7315 Edmonds St, south-west.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Cariboo

items.t: Watercourse diligence: the Cariboo and Brunette River Conservation Lands and the Stoney Creek Park and Trail System are dedicated by City park bylaw on the area's north side — for creek-side lots, check watercourse setbacks early; the setback rules travel with the creek, not the lot line.

Bare-land strata rules (applies to any bare-land strata lot, including a future stratified R1 multi-unit lot): Form B diligence (fees, amounts owed, levies, CRF balance, insurance summary; provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions (younger spouse/partner, caregivers, legacy residents, defined children); a listing's "45+" line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Cariboo ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR.

blocks.text: Good to know about Cariboo

items.t: The secondary school dates the whole lot fabric (1961): Cariboo Hill Secondary opened with 410 students because the elementary schools had outgrown Edmonds Junior High as their destination, peaked at over 1,100 students in 1974, and took additions in 1969, 1971 and 1974 — the Cariboo-Armstrong streets are a 1960s–70s subdivision fabric, which is the servicing and housing-age context for every lot on them.

The green space on the north side is conservation land, not a manicured park: the Cariboo and Brunette River Conservation Lands and the Stoney Creek Park and Trail System are dedicated by park bylaw — creek and conservation land is what borders the north-side lots, with the setback rules that travel with it.

Stratification is the quiet land story here: Burnaby's R1 rules expressly allow lots with two or more primary units to be stratified — in an area with no bare-land market, that permission, not a subdivision, is how new ground-oriented strata lots get created on Cariboo's house streets.

Jared's take on Cariboo
Cariboo ranks among Burnaby’s quieter pockets. Families buy here for the Armstrong / Cariboo Hill school pairing and the calm east-side streets rather than a town-centre address.

faq.a: In one pocket: Manchester Drive, south of Lougheed Highway. Four complexes — Barclay Woods, Brookside Court, Brookside Park and Strathmore Towers — hold the sub-area's verified apartment stock; the rest of Cariboo is detached streets, parks and conservation land.
The distinction matters because the Manchester buildings are 1981–1994 low-rise and tower stock, not new town-centre towers.
faq.q: Are the Manchester Drive buildings part of The City of Lougheed?

faq.a: Barclay Woods and Brookside Court are wood-frame; Strathmore Towers (1994) is three concrete high-rises. Brookside Park's construction type is not confirmed in the sources checked. Wood-frame versus concrete changes the insurance, depreciation-report and levy conversation — confirm the specific building on the Form B.
faq.q: Which buildings are wood-frame and which are concrete?

faq.a: Not confirmed. Unit listings state 1980; the directory page for 9867 Manchester Drive states 1981. Verify against the strata plan before relying on either year.
faq.q: Barclay Woods is listed as built in 1980 and 1981 — which is right?

faq.a: It depends on the complex. Brookside Court's published position is one cat allowed, no dogs. Barclay Woods publishes pets allowed with restrictions (one listing specifies 1 cat or 1 dog). Brookside Park and Strathmore Towers publish pets allowed. Pet bylaws remain enforceable in BC — the registered bylaws on the Form B govern.
On named, tenure-verified evidence, yes: Strathmore Lane's townhouse component on Morrey Court (strata, built 2005).
faq.q: Is there really only one townhouse complex in Cariboo?

faq.a: The directory states rentals allowed, and in any event long-term strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void province-wide since Nov 24, 2022; short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw — read the registered bylaws on the Form B package.
faq.q: Can I rent out a Strathmore Lane townhouse?

faq.a: The City is replacing the Cameron Community Centre and Library ($267 million; aquatic facility, two-court gymnasium, weight room, indoor running track, fitness studios) while a temporary centre and library operate inside The City of Lougheed — a real amenity story with a construction-period gap buyers should know about.
faq.q: What does the Cameron rebuild mean for this pocket?

faq.a: In east Burnaby around Cariboo Road and Cariboo Hill, between Lougheed Highway and the Edmonds side, anchored by Armstrong Elementary and Cariboo Hill Secondary; it is a GVR MLS® sub-area within the City of Burnaby.

It depends on the address. In-area SD41 schools include Armstrong Elementary (K–7), 8757 Armstrong Ave, Lyndhurst Elementary (K–7), 9847 Lyndhurst St, and Cariboo Hill Secondary (8–12), 8580 16th Ave; catchments are address-based and must be checked in the SD41 locator.
